solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Line on board produced by tool

definitions.meaning: in chess a ... is a vertical column of squares on the board
a rasping hand tool for smoothing metal or wood

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: a chessboard column and a metalworker's abrasive implement.

clue.text: A foreign type beastly to others?

parts.note: un is the French word for a
kind means type or sort

explanation.surface: Someone sniffs that a foreign sort behaves badly towards other people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kind' also hints at humankind, so being beastly to fellow humans is wittily the opposite of kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Cruel or harsh treatment of people is a synonym for being beastly to them.

clue.text: Short reptile, one old and decrepit from what we hear

indicators.note: this phrase says the word for something worn out is to be taken as spoken, not as spelt

parts.note: an old crock is a worn-out person or thing

explanation.surface: An elderly, broken-down creature is described as a stunted reptile.
explanation.walkthrough: A CROCK, British slang for a decrepit old person or car, sounds like the shortened name of the crocodile.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal clipped form of crocodile is a shortened name for that reptile.

clue.text: Stag hastened, in part struck with fear

indicators.note: in part says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A deer runs off quickly, frightened.
explanation.definitionFit: Being horrified and appalled is the sense of being struck with fear or dismay.

clue.text: Try very hard to meet qualification for intestinal surgery?

definitions.meaning: an informal idiom for straining every effort
read literally, having a burst bowel would qualify a patient for an operation on the gut

explanation.walkthrough: 'to meet' is just a link between the two readings.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to strain oneself to the limit; literally it describes a ruptured bowel needing an operation.

clue.text: What politicians must read? Not the FT!

definitions.text: What politicians must read? Not the FT!

parts.words: What politicians must read? Not the FT!
parts.note: a government policy document is not the Financial Times, which is printed on pink newsprint

explanation.walkthrough: The FT (Financial Times, a British newspaper) is famously pink, so the paper politicians must study is a different colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A government report setting out proposed legislation is called by this name in Britain.

clue.text: Big road's number by French sea — the label's wrong

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's major motorway, written MI, and the 's gives S
mer is the French word for sea

explanation.surface: A sign on a motorway beside the French coast has been wrongly labelled.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the main London-to-Leeds motorway; crosswords write its 1 as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrong or inaccurate name applied to something is the meaning of the word.

clue.text: Big team playing — a lot of information needed

indicators.note: a team that is playing is in action, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A major sports side in a match needs plenty of data.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of BIGTEAM gives the answer; 'needed' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of a million binary digits is a sizeable quantity of computer data.

clue.text: Awkward? That's not right for Parisian

definitions.meaning: a Parisian would say ... for left, the side that is not right

explanation.definitionFit: The English borrowing means socially clumsy; in French the word literally means left.

clue.text: Explosive by side of house for process to remove trees?

parts.note: HE is the abbreviation for high explosive
a wing is a part built out to one side of a house

explanation.surface: Blasting charges set next to a house to clear the trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Chopping with an axe is how timber is felled, so it is a method of clearing trees.

clue.text: Reduction of speed in big town is seen as a virtue

indicators.note: the shortened speed sits inside the word for a big town

parts.note: a city is a large town

indicators.note: a reduction cuts something down, here dropping the last letter of the speed word

parts.note: haste means speed

explanation.surface: Slowing down traffic in a large town is praised as a moral quality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reduction of speed' reads as traffic calming, but 'Reduction of' simply drops the last letter of the speed word; 'in' then places the result inside the big town.
explanation.definitionFit: Sexual purity is traditionally counted among the Christian moral excellences.

clue.text: Room for doubt

parts.note: the space between what is claimed and what can be believed

explanation.walkthrough: 'Room' suggests a chamber, but it means a gap: the distance between official statements and the truth.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the disparity between claims made and how far people trust them.

clue.text: Little relative gainfully employed or back in education?

parts.note: rel. is a short form of relative
earning means being paid for work

explanation.surface: A small relation who has a paying job, or one who has returned to school.
explanation.definitionFit: Studying again something once known is being back in education, as the playful definition suggests.

clue.text: No honey served up — fruit is on offer

indicators.note: in a down clue, served up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: mel is Latin for honey, used in pharmacy

explanation.surface: No honey is served, but some fruit is offered instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' turns NOMEL around; 'is on offer' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharp yellow citrus is a familiar example of a fruit.

clue.text: Smear with colour, not quite right

indicators.note: not quite means the colour word falls one letter short of complete

parts.note: blue is a colour

explanation.surface: Daubing paint on something that isn't quite correct.
explanation.definitionFit: To smudge or make indistinct is to smear, as with wet paint or ink.

clue.text: Herd moved across river and put in new shed?

indicators.note: the jumbled herd letters stretch across the river, holding it inside
a herd that is moved is shifted about, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: the Ouse is a river in England

explanation.surface: Cattle are driven over a river and housed in a fresh barn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moved' gives REHD from the herd's letters, and 'across' wraps them round the Ouse, a river in Yorkshire and East Anglia.
explanation.definitionFit: To provide with fresh lodging is the sense, and a shed is wittily a home for animals.

clue.text: Tiny lad with idea not half afraid to speak out?

parts.note: Tiny Tim is the crippled boy in Dickens's A Christmas Carol

indicators.note: not half means only the first half of the word idea is kept

explanation.surface: A small boy with a notion is rather too scared to voice it.
explanation.walkthrough: Tiny Tim is the sickly boy in Dickens's A Christmas Carol; half of IDEA gives ID.
explanation.definitionFit: Shy and lacking courage, so reluctant to say what one thinks.

clue.text: Old country residence opening 24 hours

indicators.note: the residence opens up the 24-hour word and sits within it

parts.note: a day lasts 24 hours
home is a residence

explanation.surface: A rural house in the old style open day and night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old country residence' reads as a quaint cottage, but 'Old country' alone is the definition: Dahomey was the former name of Benin in West Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: The West African nation now named Benin bore this name until 1975.

clue.text: Record binder

definitions.meaning: to ... something is to record it

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to capture sound on a recorder and an adhesive strip that fastens.

clue.text: Guess this could suggest a midnight murder

definitions.meaning: a wild attempt at an answer with no information

definitions.text: this could suggest a midnight murder
definitions.meaning: literally, a gunshot fired at night

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means an uninformed guess; taken literally it is a gun fired in darkness.

clue.text: Woman in residence wanting drink brought round

indicators.note: the residence abbreviation goes inside the drink
the drink is wrapped around the residence abbreviation

parts.note: tea is a drink

explanation.surface: A lady at home who wants someone to fetch her a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting' is only a link; 'in' and 'brought round' both signal the drink enclosing the residence abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Teresa is a female given name, so it fits a clue asking for a woman.

clue.text: Bradman's famous duck?

definitions.meaning: the great Australian cricketer Sir ... Bradman, known as Don

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a duck is a score of nought, which Bradman famously made in his last Test innings, so the surface tempts a cricket reading.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both the first name of the Australian batsman Bradman and of Disney's cartoon duck.

clue.text: Asked to finish, having penned several sheets

indicators.note: to pen is to enclose, so the finish word holds the sheets inside

parts.note: to end is to finish
a quire is a set of 24 or 25 sheets of paper

explanation.surface: Someone was told to wrap up after writing out a few pages.
explanation.definitionFit: To make an inquiry is to put a question, so the past form matches asked.

clue.text: A number or twice as many in overnight accommodation

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500
taken as written
M is the Roman numeral for 1000, twice 500

explanation.surface: One guest or double that number staying in shared lodgings for the night.
explanation.definitionFit: A dormitory is a sleeping room, informally shortened, used for overnight stays.

clue.text: Butcher offers prime bit of meat — and fish!

indicators.note: the prime, or first, bit of the word meat is its opening letter

parts.note: to angle is to fish

explanation.surface: A butcher sells top-quality cuts of meat and some fish too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butcher' looks like a person behind the counter, but it is a verb meaning to mutilate.
explanation.definitionFit: To mutilate or ruin something badly is to butcher it, as a verb.

clue.text: Behold saints making sacrifice?

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning behold

explanation.surface: Look at the holy martyrs giving up their lives.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving something up means one is deprived of it, so a sacrifice involves a deprivation.

clue.text: Messengers providing brief answer set to be detained

indicators.note: the set word is held within the brief answer, like someone kept in custody

parts.note: ans. is the abbreviation for answer
to gel is to set, as jelly does

explanation.surface: Couriers supply a quick reply that sets someone to be held.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek word angelos means messenger, and angels are God's heralds in scripture.

clue.text: Cavalier man having celebrity status

parts.note: Roy is a man's name
the A-list is the top tier of celebrities

explanation.surface: A carefree fellow who has become famous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cavalier' looks like an adjective for offhand, but here it is a supporter of Charles I in the English Civil War.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cavaliers were the king's supporters in the English Civil War, loyal to the crown.
